Normally: no. Your phone uses one connection at a time, and Android decides which. NetPilot watches both and tells you when Wi-Fi stops working.

With "Use both together" on: each new connection goes over Wi-Fi or mobile data, shared out by their speed. Many connections at once (web pages, app updates, several apps) get faster. One single connection, like one video or a video call, still uses one network: joining both for a single connection needs a server in the middle, which NetPilot doesn't use.

Some ads come from the same address as the video or page itself (YouTube is a common example). No DNS blocker can remove those without breaking the content.

NetPilot works entirely on your phone. No account, no ads, no analytics, no crash reports. Your activity list never leaves the phone. Lookups go encrypted to the DNS provider you chose above. Block lists are downloaded from public sources.

• A website or app won't load: pause protection for 5 minutes. If it works then, allow that website, or let the app skip protection.

• Protection keeps turning off: allow NetPilot to run in the background (Settings tab), and turn on Always on.

• "Another VPN is on": Android allows only one VPN at a time. Turn the other one off.

• Wi-Fi says connected but nothing loads: check the Connection tab. NetPilot shows what's wrong and how to fix it.

• Ads still show in some apps: some ads come from the same address as the content. DNS blocking can't remove those.

• Blocking seems to do nothing: set Private DNS to Automatic, and turn off "Use secure DNS" with a custom provider in your browser. Both send lookups around NetPilot.
NetPilot %1$s. Block lists by: %2$s. Lists are downloaded at runtime under their own licences.
NetPilot blocks ads, trackers and harmful websites in all your apps, right on your phone. No account, no subscription.

NetPilot watches Wi-Fi and mobile data and tells you when Wi-Fi is "connected" but not working.\n\nIf you want, it can also use both at once: for downloads in NetPilot, and (experimental) by sharing your apps\' connections between them. One single connection, like one video, still uses one network.

Android will ask to let NetPilot set up a VPN. NetPilot uses it only to check website names on your phone; your browsing isn\'t sent to any NetPilot server.\n\nNotifications let NetPilot tell you about connection problems.
Android uses the VPN permission for any app that filters connections. NetPilot keeps everything on your phone. Tap Connect to try again.
Android allows one VPN at a time. Turning on NetPilot will turn the other VPN off.

On. New connections are shared between Wi-Fi and mobile data by their speed.
Use Wi-Fi and mobile data together?

Every connection from your apps will pass through NetPilot and go out over Wi-Fi or mobile data.

• Faster when many things load at once: web pages, app updates, several apps.
• Not faster for one single connection, such as one video or a video call.
• Uses mobile data even when Wi-Fi works. Android will treat your connection as mobile data, so big automatic downloads wait.
• Uses more battery.
• "Ping" tools won't work while this is on.

You can turn it off any time.
